newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Tel Aviv bourse makes listing changes.
newsitem.headline: Tel Aviv bourse makes listing changes.

text.p: The Tel Aviv Stock Exchange said on Tuesday it was lowering the amount of equity capital needed by new companies before their listing on the exchange from $3 million to $1 million.

The measure is part of a liberalisation package approved by the exchange's board to align its regulations with those accepted worldwide. The changes are meant to increase the level of tradability of the bourse, the exchange said.

While lowering the amount of equity capital needed, small companies issuing less than $6 million will need to have public holdings of at least 30 to 40 percent instead of the previously needed 25 percent, the exchange said.
The bourse said it was also allowing companies to issue a greater variety of bonds to include mortgage-backed bonds and bonds backed by other financial instruments.
Companies issuing bonds need to have after-listing capital of $4 million instead of $6 million, the exchange said.
